draft.rationale: migrationProgress now parses the counters JSON inside a catch that returns 0, so a corrupt or truncated payload reports 0% progress exactly like a migration that has not started; the caller cannot tell the parse failed.

The subscribe path now funnels every save through a catch that only logs when NODE_ENV is not production, so in production a failing persist is dropped and nothing above the subscription learns that the cache was not written.
restartContentLayer logs a content-layer sync failure and the restart resolves as successful, so the dev server runs with no content collections and only a console line records why.

connectEphemeralClient catches the ready-wait failure of the Redis client and only warns, then boot continues; the process runs with an unconnected client and callers see plain failures later instead of a failed start.

close() for an adapter without a port now awaits Promise.allSettled over every namespace adapter and never inspects the results, so an adapter that failed to close is discarded and the caller believes the server closed cleanly.

The lookup-sort validation resolves the related model inside a catch that sets relatedModelId to undefined, which then skips the whole validation; a failed read turns an invalid sort column into an accepted one.

The new pubsub demux parses the message inside an empty catch that keeps the raw string, and wraps every handler in a catch that only logs, so a corrupt payload or a throwing subscriber loses the message with no failure reaching the publisher.
ensureLinkedRecordMetas returns from an empty catch when a meta load fails, so the linked-record title stays empty and nothing distinguishes a missing table from a failed load.
verifyTotp now wraps the otplib load and the synchronous verify in a catch-all that returns false, so a missing or broken otplib module is reported as a wrong code instead of as an error.

getScopeAncestors converts a failed View lookup into null and continues with base-only ancestors, so a read error silently narrows the ancestor chain the command registry uses to discard stale undone rows.
emit() now attaches a catch that logs and drops a listener rejection, so a throwing event listener loses its failure in a log line while the emitting code continues as though every listener ran.
The result of onConfirm is given a catch whose body is only a comment, so a rejected confirm action disappears; nothing in the flow reaches a user or a caller.
ackThread treats any failure of the family check as a denial and returns the family thread id, so the caller acknowledges another thread's events instead of reporting the failed check.

The serialized prefs write catches its failure, logs it, and clears the bookkeeping ref, so a prompt preference that never reached the server is retried silently and the user sees a prompt that keeps coming back with no error.
runHandler forwards a handler error to the application's onError event and rethrows when there is none, so the failure reaches whoever registered the handler; a boundary that reports, not a swallow.
The decode catch converts a base64 decoding failure into JwtTokenInvalid, a typed failure the caller already handles for every other invalid token.
The body is read from a clone and a non-JSON or empty body skips prettifying while the original response is returned untouched; the response the client gets still carries its real content.
A caller that joins a failed derivation drops the cache entry and derives again, and the second failure is returned to that caller; the rejection is not converted into a value.
The new catches are narrow: malformed percent-encoding becomes a 400 response, and toFilePath returns undefined only for ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH while rethrowing everything else.
The caught import failure is rethrown as AstroError with the cause attached; the edit adds the cause, it does not hide the fault.
Only the binding's 9412 transform error becomes a 400 response for the requested href; any other error is rethrown to the caller.
The standalone entrypoint reports a failed start with console.error and exits with code 1, a visible outcome for the process.
Only ENOENT from stat of a dangling symlink is skipped; every other error is rethrown, and the skipped entry is one that cannot exist.
Unlocking is described and implemented as never throwing: the operating system releases the lock at process exit, so a failed unlock cannot change the result.
A Conf initialization that fails on permissions yields null and disables telemetry; the preference store is a best-effort side channel, and the class already treated a null store as disabled.
The new catch removes the stored files and then throws BadRequestException, and the inner catch during that cleanup only serves a request that already fails.
Both catches undo the partially inserted modules and rethrow the original error, so the failure still reaches the caller with the container left consistent.
The .catch(() => []) on the thread listing predates this edit, which only routes the call through a shared listing helper; the swallow is untouched debt.
The edit narrows a catch that returned null for every error so that it returns null only for UnauthorizedException and rethrows the rest, which removes the swallow the scope had.
The lock and cache catches that log and continue were already in getData and setData; the edit under review swaps the Redis client and skips the lock while Redis is not ready.
The before code already folded every authentication failure into joining the public room; the edit rewrites the same behaviour as .catch(() => false), so the concern is old and unchanged.
Each per-payment refund is caught only so the remaining seats are still attempted, and the collected errors are thrown afterwards as one aggregate error for the caller.
The FormData conversion failure is returned as { revalidated: false, error } and also reported through onError, so the caller receives the failure in a checked shape.
Failing to write the scrubbed payload to web storage is a quota or read-only condition, and the function still returns the scrubbed value the caller asked for.
The edit only widens the character class used to escape the realm in the challenge header; the ?? picks the request URL for an optional option.
The ?? selects the factory's default application options when the caller passes none; nothing here handles a failure.
The ?? supplies an empty string when the request has no Accept-Encoding header, which is the genuine absence of the header.
The ?? falls back to the other spelling of the quality parameter, a case-insensitive header name, not a failed read.
The ??= memoizes one project-info promise per telemetry instance, so concurrent callers share one derivation.
The ?? takes the injected trace function when the caller supplies one and imports the real module otherwise; the new warning handler only reports unresolvable modules.
The ?? gives the generator empty params when the caller passes none before sanitizing them.
The ?? builds a codec descriptor from the column id when the column carries no codec object, an optional field.
The ?? gives an empty meta for a view that has no meta yet; the parse helper already returns an empty object for a corrupt meta, and the edit spreads that value into the insert.
The ?? only changes the default of an optional create field from true to false; no failure is being handled.
The edit adds a catch that keeps no trace of a failed progress push and returns the pending count as if the device were in sync. The scan flow keeps working from a stale snapshot and nobody is told.
A failed charge now falls through an empty catch, so the account is scheduled for a retry that reads as a successful attempt, and a declined card looks like an ordinary dunning step.

The archive write fails silently and the method still returns the target path, so a caller that later reads that path gets a missing file with no hint that the write failed. The catch turns a permission fault into an apparent success.
The new try block wraps the whole row write and the empty catch drops the failure, so a payslip can be missing from the export while the byte count still looks plausible.
An empty catch replaces an explanatory one, dropping the device from the refreshed list with nothing said. A revoked token or an unreachable service disables push for that device silently.
A failed push is logged and then marked synced, so the contact is never retried and the report counts it as pushed. The warning is the only trace, and the sync runs as if it succeeded.

The new catch logs a failed write of the alert bookkeeping record and the loop carries on as if the alert had been tracked. The cooldown then misfires on every later run and no one is told the record was lost.

A failed reminder now returns true after logging, so the job counts the invoice as reminded and bumps nothing. The error line is written for an operator who is not reading the log while the run reports success.

The read failure is logged and replaced by an empty row list, after which the worker replaces the stored window with nothing and moves the watermark past it. The rollup loses a whole window and reports normal progress.
The debit is wrapped in a catch that writes an error line and continues to credit the destination, so money appears on both sides and the caller sees a completed transfer.
A failed discount lookup now returns an empty list, so the quote is built at full price and looks like a customer with no discounts. The revenue difference is invisible to the caller.
A failed readdir is turned into an empty listing, and the editor then shows an empty folder. A permission or mount fault reads as a folder with no files.

When the rate table cannot be fetched or parsed, the loader returns an empty table, and every quote comes back as zero with no surcharge. Free shipping is a plausible normal result that hides the fault.
A failed session lookup is reported as null, the same value as an absent session, so a database fault is served as an anonymous visitor and the request continues.
The edited catch drops the warning and returns zero on hand, so a failed count read becomes a full reorder suggestion. The planner then buys stock the warehouse already holds.
Rows that fail to parse now fall back to an empty list through the undefined branch, so a corrupt statement reconciles to zero balances and the report reads as a clean period.
The parsed reading is recomputed with a zero fallback on the raw field, so a value the parser already rejected is billed as zero units and the customer is not charged for real consumption.
A payload that fails to decode is replaced by a zero measurement, which the box chooser accepts as fitting the smallest box. An unusable measurement therefore ships as a successful choice.
The refresh now catches the decode failure and keeps the previous empty table, so every later quote throws for a missing rule or uses nothing. The caller cannot tell the rules were never loaded.

The edit inspects the failure result only to log it and then mails the statement anyway, reporting success. A rejected save leaves no record and the customer holds a statement the system does not have.

The new line counts the rejected settlements but only writes the count into an error log, and the method returns the fulfilled rows as the export total. A failed region is a missing section of the export that the caller accepts as complete.
The edit reads the failure result and then returns the same bumped draft on both branches, so an autosave that the store rejected is reported to the caller as the new draft.
Rejected transports are counted and logged, then dropped from the total that the caller treats as delivered. The delivery failures reach nobody who can retry them.
A store that declines the put is only logged, and the method deletes the source file regardless. The attachment is gone from both places while the caller sees a routine archive.
The edit stops turning a decline into a returned string and rethrows a typed decline instead, so the caller must handle it. Every branch either throws a domain error or returns the captured outcome.
The added catch wraps the cause in a typed failure and throws it on, so the loop never continues past a failed upload and the caller sees the fault.
The function contract is null when the settings file is absent, and the catch is narrowed to ENOENT while everything else is thrown on. A missing file is an expected absence, not a hidden fault.
This is a search box whose contract is that unparsable input is simply not a filter, and the empty catch covers only the parser on user text. Invalid typing is the expected case.
The added branch only spells out the null that newest already returns, and the directory read throws anything that is not a missing directory. An empty backup folder is a normal state.
The catch wraps a metrics emission only, which happens after the render result is computed and cannot change it. Telemetry that is dropped is the best-effort case.
The catch wraps a write into a cache whose contents are rebuilt from the source on the next read, and the page itself is already in hand. Losing the cache write cannot change the result.
This is closing a read handle inside a finally block after the tally is complete and stored. A close that fails changes nothing about the summary the caller receives.
The catch sits at the request boundary: it logs, answers 500 and the client sees a failed upload. The error is turned into a visible outcome, which the boundary exception allows.
This is a job runner top level that turns a step failure into a recorded failed step and writes it out, so the operator sees which step broke. The step result propagates to the exit code.
The catch is in a UI event handler and moves the form into a visible failed state with a message for the user. The failure reaches the person who can act on it.
The added catch is in a test-harness path of a spec file, where an unreadable item is meant to be reported as unavailable to the test. Test code is outside the rule.
The whole file is a test helper for pricing specs, and the added catch keeps a malformed fixture from failing an unrelated assertion. Test code is the exception here.
This file only exists to build fixtures for batch tests, and the catch marks a batch the fixture could not summarise. Nothing in production reads it.
The send already returns false on any failure with nothing said, and the edit only adds a read accessor for the sent set. The swallow is untouched, so this edit neither introduces nor widens it.
The null return on a failed remote read predates the edit, which adds an unrelated accessor. The existing debt stays, so the concern is present but the edit does not hide anything new.
Before, a rejected config quietly became an empty endpoint and the device polled nowhere. The edit rethrows a typed config error, so the caller must handle it and the fault is visible.
The report used to warn and count a failed fetch as zero units, so a broken account looked unused. The edit removes the catch and lets the failure reach the caller.
The added fallback covers a parameter the caller may omit, and absence there is a normal call shape rather than a failed operation. Nothing hides a fault.
The new catch names the path, keeps the cause and throws a typed error, so a missing or malformed manifest still reaches the caller with more detail than before.
The edit adds a switch that maps a closed settlement state to a label and never swallows anything. It is plain formatting of a value the caller already holds.
A failed seat count becomes a rejected outcome with a reason, which the callers of reserve already handle by their discriminated union. The failure is reported, not swallowed.
The added helper computes the longest session in a room from slots already in memory. There is no I/O and no failure path, so there is nothing to hide.
The new drain returns the reasons for every rejected payload alongside the accepted count, so a malformed job is reported rather than dropped.
The edit makes sure the lock is released exactly once on either path and rethrows the work error. The failure still reaches the caller and the finally stays as the last resort.
The catch compensates the half-applied move and rethrows, so a failed transfer neither leaves stock behind nor passes as success. The error is preserved for the caller.
